cards.explanation: The answer is False, friends. The torrent doesn't stop at open land. The LORD says it will overflow “…the land and its fullness, the cities and their inhabitants.” The cities and the people living in them are right in the picture (Jeremiah 47:2).

The answer is cry out and wail, friends. The LORD says, “The people will cry out, and all who dwell in the land will wail” (Jeremiah 47:2). It isn't only a few folks, either. All who dwell in the land are in that sentence.

The answer is galloping horses and rumbling chariots, friends. The wailing comes at the sound of “…the galloping hooves of stallions, the rumbling of chariots, and the clatter of their wheels” (Jeremiah 47:3). That's three sounds stacked up in one line. Hooves, rumbling and clattering, all headed their way.

The answer is False, friends, and it's a sober one. The LORD says, “The fathers will not turn back for their sons; their hands will hang limp” (Jeremiah 47:3). The fathers don't turn back, and their hands hang limp. I'll just let that line sit for a second.

The answer is the LORD, friends. The text says, “Indeed, the LORD is about to destroy the Philistines…” (Jeremiah 47:4). The whole word in this passage comes from Him. It begins with “This is what the LORD says…” and it stays His word all the way through (Jeremiah 47:2).

The answer is mourning, friends. The text says, “The people of Gaza will shave their heads in mourning…” (Jeremiah 47:5). This is a day of grief for them. I think this one hurts, so I'll let the verse speak for itself.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, “Ashkelon will be silenced” (Jeremiah 47:5). Ashkelon comes up again at the end of the passage too, where the LORD has appointed the sword against it (Jeremiah 47:7). It's a city the word keeps coming back to.

The answer is to go back in its sheath and be still, friends. The cry says, “Return to your sheath; cease and be still!” (Jeremiah 47:6). It sounds like a plea for the sword to stop. And the very next verse answers it, so keep listening.

The answer is commanded, friends. The verse asks, “How can it rest when the LORD has commanded it?” (Jeremiah 47:7). The sword's work comes from His command. That's the answer to the plea in the verse before.
